name: Agent-as-a-Graph: Knowledge Graph-Based Tool and Agent Retrieval for LLM Multi-Agent Systems
venue: arXiv preprint (arXiv:2511.18194 [cs.CL]); not peer-reviewed at time of writing
authors_affiliation: Faheem Nizar, Elias Lumer, Anmol Gulati, Pradeep Honaganahalli Basavaraju, Vamse Kumar Subbiah — Commercial Technology and Innovation Office, PricewaterhouseCoopers (PwC), U.S.
code_url: N/A (no official code repository linked in the arXiv listing or paper; the paper notes the KG is stored in standard graph backends compatible with Cypher/Neo4j but releases no code)
task_domain: tool-use / agent routing (tool and parent-agent retrieval for LLM multi-agent systems with MCP servers)
problem_setting: Offline retrieval/selection problem within a multi-agent system: a single orchestrator must route a user query (or its decomposed sub-steps) to the correct executable subagent among hundreds/thousands of agents, each bundling tens to hundreds of MCP-server tools. The retrievable store is a static, offline-induced bipartite knowledge graph of agents and tools built from existing MCP manifests/schemas; there is no online growth, no agent execution rollout, and supervision is limited to ground-truth agent-tool mappings used only for evaluation (the retriever itself is training-free/non-learned).
what_is_retrieved: Tools (MCP tool nodes) and their parent agents (MCP server nodes); the final returned set is the top-K executable agents reached via tool-to-agent graph traversal.
retrieval_grounding: STATIC external corpus — a bipartite knowledge graph of agents and tools auto-induced offline from MCP manifests/schemas; no growing/episodic memory written by the agent.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Fixed top-K ranking objective (top-K unique executable agents); evaluated with Recall@K / mAP@K / nDCG@K at K in {1,3,5,(10)}. It aims to recover the complete set of relevant agents within a fixed K rather than a precision-driven variable-size set, but is not framed as minimal-set completeness recovery.
cbr_cycle_coverage: N/A (not a case-based reasoning method; only a Retrieve-like step exists, no Reuse/Revise/Retain)
explicit_cbr_grounding: False — the work does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner; it is a knowledge-graph RAG retrieval method.
retrieval_unit: tool-API node (tool name + description) and agent/MCP-server node (agent name + description), organized as a bipartite KG-subgraph; the retrieved/returned unit is the parent agent (tool-API granularity at index time, agent granularity at output).
index_source: Static corpus, offline-induced: the agent-tool bipartite knowledge graph is automatically constructed offline from existing MCP server manifests and tool schemas; frozen at query time (no online/test-time induction).
index_structure_topology: Bipartite dependency/knowledge GRAPH G=(A,T,E) where tool nodes are linked to their parent agent (owner) nodes via ownership metadata edges; both node types embedded in a shared/unified vector space and stored in standard graph backends (Cypher/Neo4j-compatible). Hierarchical agent->tool ownership relation.
retriever_type: Hybrid — dense vector search over a unified embedding space for both tool and agent nodes (eight embedding models evaluated), combined with graph traversal; BM25 used only as a baseline. No learned/LLM reranker.
retriever_learning_signal: None (off-the-shelf) — the retriever uses pretrained embedding models with no fine-tuning; ranking uses a training-free, non-learned type-specific weighted Reciprocal Rank Fusion with interpretable, manually-set type priors (alpha_A, alpha_T). The paper explicitly contrasts this with learned/LLM re-rankers.
query_construction: Two paradigms: (1) Direct Querying uses the raw user high-level question; (2) Step-wise Querying decomposes the query into sub-tasks and submits each step independently. Step-wise decomposition (reasoning-based retrieval planning) is the primary evaluation setting.
query_granularity: Both task-level (Direct Querying, one-shot at t=0) and step/sub-task-level (Step-wise Querying); the step/sub-task level is the primary setting.
when_to_retrieve: Iterative in the primary (step-wise) setting — retrieval is invoked once per decomposed sub-step; one-shot in the Direct Querying setting. Decomposition is via a fixed schedule of sub-steps, not an uncertainty-triggered or learned router.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Fixed schedule — retrieval fires per decomposed sub-step (one retrieval call per step) or once for the whole task in direct mode; there is no token-confidence, attention, learned-complexity, or reflection-token trigger.
reranking: Yes — a type-specific weighted Reciprocal Rank Fusion (wRRF). After forming a unified candidate list with a global base rank r(e), each entity is scored alpha_T/(k+r(e)) for tool nodes or alpha_A/(k+r(e)) for agent nodes (k=60), reranked, then top-K unique agents selected via graph traversal. This is a non-learned, interpretable reranking (not a cross-encoder or instruction-tuned reranker).
retrieved_context_refinement: Rerank only — type-specific wRRF reranking followed by tool->agent graph traversal and deduplication to the top-K unique executable agents; no decomposition-recompose, distillation, distractor filtering, or compression of retrieved content.
tool_document_engineering: Raw name+description fields — tool nodes index tool names and descriptions; agent nodes index agent/MCP server names and descriptions. No synthetic-query augmentation, expansion, or instruction-tuned tool embeddings; an agent-only baseline dataset is constructed using only MCP server names+descriptions to isolate tool-level information.
index_content_separation: Partial — lightweight retrievable name/description nodes are indexed and linked via graph edges to their parent agent, which carries heavier execution context (authentication, parameter inference, access policies) surfaced through traversal; but there is no explicit progressive-disclosure / SOP-index-then-content load-on-demand mechanism described.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: Static index over MCP servers/tools integrated via the Model Context Protocol (MCP); auto-induced from MCP manifests/schemas and stored in Cypher/Neo4j-compatible backends. No live CRUD auto-synchronization is claimed (contrasts with ScaleMCP's dynamic auto-sync).
tool_dependency_awareness: Models the tool->parent-agent ownership relation as a bipartite KG and traverses tool-to-agent edges to preserve bundle context, but does not model inter-tool dependencies (output-of-A feeds B, shared auth as data-flow, prerequisites) for sequencing.
how_retrieved_used: The retrieved top-K agents are used for agent routing/selection (which executable subagent the orchestrator delegates to); evaluation is retrieval-only (retrieved agents vs ground-truth agents). Not prompt-augmentation/skill-reuse/training-signal use; it is a selection/routing output.
planning_integration: Retrieve-then-route, interleaved with query decomposition: in the primary step-wise setting the query is decomposed into sub-steps and a retrieval is run per sub-step to identify the relevant agent(s), aligning retrieval with reasoning-based planning; no MCTS/tree search or explicit plan generation is performed by the method itself.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-step (per decomposed sub-task) in the primary setting; per-answer/per-task in the Direct Querying setting.
adaptation_mechanism: N/A (not a CBR/case-adaptation method; retrieved agents are returned for routing without case revision)
retrieved_item_representation: Structured graph nodes (agent and tool name+description) surfaced as a ranked set of executable agents; not raw trajectories, distilled strategies, programs, or latent tokens.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Two-level: fine-grained tool-API capability (single tool description) at the node level and coarser agent/MCP-server capability (parent bundle) at the output level; no distilled strategy/insight, workflow, or procedural skill.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Type-specific weighting (alpha_A, alpha_T) as transparent knobs to bias toward agent coverage vs tool specificity, stabilizing top-K routing; RRF's rank-based (calibration-insensitive) fusion is robust across heterogeneous embedding signals. No retriever-aware training, relevance evaluator, self-reflection, or distractor-aware SFT.
memory_type: graph (static bipartite agent-tool knowledge graph). No episodic/skill-library/procedural memory that grows.
write_back: False — no new experiences/cases/skills are written back; the KG is built offline and frozen during retrieval.
online_growth: No — the retrievable store does not grow during deployment/test-time; it is induced offline from MCP manifests and remains static (the paper mentions Cypher/CRUD-compatible backends but no online growth is part of the method).
write_back_trigger: Never — there is no write-back mechanism; nothing is stored to memory during operation.
failure_experience_usage: N/A — no experiences (success or failure) are stored or retrieved; the method is a static retrieval over a fixed KG.
memory_evolution_update: N/A — entries are not mutated after construction (static graph; effectively append-only/none at build time only).
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No — retrieval/selection is a fixed similarity top-N followed by training-free type-specific wRRF and deterministic graph traversal; not an RL/learned policy.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: Single shared KG indexing all agents/tools in one multi-agent system used by the orchestrator for routing; not framed as memory/experience sharing across heterogeneous agent frameworks. The graph is a shared routing index rather than shared learned experience.
benchmarks: LiveMCPBench (70 MCP servers, 527 tools, 95 real-world questions annotated with step-by-step breakdowns and relevant agent-tool mappings; avg 2.68 steps, 2.82 tools, 1.40 MCP agents per question). An agent-only baseline dataset (MCP server names+descriptions only) is also constructed.
benchmark_family: tool (MCP tool/agent retrieval) — LiveMCPBench (MCP server/tool retrieval benchmark)
baselines: BM25 (lexical, via LlamaIndex BM25 retriever); Q.Retrieval (query/dense retrieval); standard RRF (Reciprocal Rank Fusion); MCPZero (active tool discovery); ScaleMCP (dynamic auto-synchronizing MCP retriever) — the last two are the prior state-of-the-art agent retrievers.
key_metrics: Recall@K, mean average precision mAP@K, normalized discounted cumulative gain nDCG@K, for K in {1,3,5} (Table 1 header also references {1,5,10}). Retrieved agents are compared against ground-truth agents.
headline_result: On LiveMCPBench, Agent-as-a-Graph (optimal type-specific weighting alpha_A=1.5, alpha_T=1.0) achieves Recall@5 = 0.85 and nDCG@5 = 0.48, a 14.9% and 14.6% improvement over prior state-of-the-art retrievers; against MCPZero's Recall@5 0.70 the unweighted variant reaches 0.83 (+18.6%), and on average across 8 embedding models 0.85 vs 0.70 (+19.4%). wRRF type-weighting adds 2.41% over standard RRF.
ablations: (1) Type-weighting ratio sweep (Table 3 / Figure 2): unweighted (1,1) gives Recall@5 0.83; optimal modest agent emphasis (alpha_A=1.5, alpha_T=1.0) gives 0.85/nDCG@5 0.47; tool-dominant (1:3) gives 0.80; aggressive agent bias (3:1) degrades to 0.76; type-specific wRRF (Eq.3) beats standard weighted RRF (Eq.2, Recall@5 ~0.79-0.80) by ~2.41%. (2) Cross-architecture generalization across 8 embedding models (Table 2): consistent gains, low variance (std ~0.02 Recall@5, ~0.01 nDCG@5); strongest on Amazon Titan v2 (0.66->0.85, +28.8%); All-MiniLM-L6-v2 0.67->0.80 (+19.4%). (3) Node-source attribution: 39.13% of retrieved top-K items originate from agent nodes; 34.44% of matched tool nodes trace back to agents via graph edges, showing both node types contribute.
evaluation_decoupling: Evaluation is intrinsic retrieval-only (Recall@K / mAP@K / nDCG@K of retrieved agents vs ground-truth agents); there is no end-to-end task-execution (e.g., task success) metric, so intrinsic and downstream metrics are not jointly decoupled — only retrieval metrics are reported.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Process/retrieval-quality only — measures retrieval accuracy (Recall/mAP/nDCG) and an analysis of which node types contribute; does not score final task outcome/success of executed agents.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Argues for efficiency qualitatively: training-free, non-learned type-specific wRRF avoids expensive LLM re-ranking and retraining; works with compact open-source embeddings (All-MiniLM-L6-v2 reaches Recall@5 0.80), valuable when embedding choice is constrained by cost/latency/licensing. No concrete latency/throughput/API-cost numbers are reported.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed-k selection: retrieve top-N (N >> K) nodes by semantic similarity, rerank via type-specific wRRF (k=60 damping constant), then return top-K unique agents (K in {1,3,5}); reranked-then-truncated. No token/prompt budget for injected content is reported (output is the agent set, not prompt-injected content).
benchmark_construction_and_size: Uses (does not construct) LiveMCPBench: 70 MCP servers, 527 tools, 95 human-annotated real-world questions with step-by-step breakdowns and ground-truth agent-tool mappings; avg 2.68 steps / 2.82 tools / 1.40 MCP agents per question. The authors additionally build a derived agent-only baseline dataset (server names+descriptions only) to isolate tool-level information.
builds_on: Reciprocal Rank Fusion (Cormack et al.) and weighted RRF; dense embedding retrievers and BM25; MCP-based tool/agent retrieval (ScaleMCP, MCPZero, ToolShed, MemTool, GraphRAG-Tool Fusion by overlapping authors); Graph RAG literature (graph-retrieval-augmented generation surveys, GraphRAG, G-Retriever, Think-on-Graph, Graph-CoT); tool-graph methods (ToolNet, ControlLLM, Graph-ToolFormer).
contrasts_with: Agent-only retrievers that match a query against a single agent description and operate only within that agent (e.g., LiveMCPBench's own retriever, AnyTool, MetaTool); tool-only retrievers that treat each tool independently and ignore bundle context (ToolShed, MCPZero-style); ScaleMCP's concatenation of agent+tool descriptions in one vector space (multi-hop limitation); heavy LLM re-rankers and corrective RAG pipelines (replaced by transparent non-learned type-specific weighting).
lineage: Group E (tool-use): graph/hierarchical tool-and-agent retrieval for MCP-based multi-agent systems. Positioned in the 2024-2025 tool-retrieval lineage that moved from flat dense tool retrieval to graph/hierarchical and MCP-dynamic indices, extending GraphRAG-Tool Fusion / ScaleMCP / MCPZero by jointly modeling agents and tools as co-equal KG nodes with type-specific wRRF reranking and tool-to-agent traversal.
